title: Pictures that carry information
statement: Prefer a picture that carries information, such as a map or a comparison chart, to one that only decorates.
detail: Review of generated articles kept asking to swap an image that only illustrates for one that carries information: a chart comparing two plans or two positions (`icloud-work/k_12_social_studies/ap_files/Articles Tracker.xlsx`, sheet 'APUSH Articles', cell M17), a map of a compromise in place of a second image (cell M34), and a chart or table comparing two movements at that point in the text (sheet 'Sheet3', cell A19). The note in M17 also objected that two images were placed back to back in the article. Put each picture beside the text it supports.

evidence.quote: The two images are placed back to back in the article.
This should include a map that shows the Missouri Compromise. I would recommend eliminating the 2 image in favor of it.
It would be most efficient for the reader to see a chart/table here actually comparing the two movements characteristics
A generic fantasy trailer, decorative mascot, stock montage, old geology clip or slide of the final answer does not satisfy the new units' media needs.
During teaching, switch to clear, labelled maps, character relationships and quotations.
